reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / standard rheumatology references
clinicalPearls: An autosomal dominant granulomatous autoinflammatory disorder caused by gain-of-function mutations in the NOD2 (CARD15) gene
Classically presents in early childhood with a triad of granulomatous arthritis, dermatitis, and uveitis
The arthritis is polyarticular with characteristic boggy synovial and tenosynovial swelling and cysts
Skin involvement is a persistent scaly or ichthyosis-like granulomatous rash
Ocular disease is typically a chronic, often bilateral granulomatous uveitis that can threaten sight
The sporadic phenotypically identical form is termed early-onset sarcoidosis, but unlike classic sarcoidosis the lungs and hilar nodes are usually spared
Non-caseating granulomas are found on biopsy of affected skin or synovium, and NOD2 genetic testing confirms the diagnosis
Management uses corticosteroids and steroid-sparing immunosuppression, with TNF and IL-1 directed biologics for refractory disease
reference.pathophysiology: Gain-of-function mutations in NOD2, an intracellular pattern-recognition receptor of the innate immune system, cause constitutive activation of NF-kB signalling independent of the usual microbial ligand. This drives spontaneous granuloma formation and chronic inflammation affecting joints, skin, and eyes. NOD2 is the same gene implicated (with different variants) in Crohn disease, though the mechanisms differ.
additionalDifferentials: Other causes of childhood chronic uveitis
additionalInvestigations: Biopsy of skin or synovium demonstrating non-caseating granulomas
Slit-lamp and dilated ophthalmological examination for granulomatous uveitis
Exclusion of infective and classic sarcoid causes of granulomas
Acute-phase reactants and imaging of affected joints
redFlags: Sight-threatening uveitis with complications such as cataract, glaucoma, or macular oedema
Progressive joint destruction and deformity from chronic granulomatous synovitis
Atypical multiorgan involvement (large-vessel or visceral) in severe variants
Diagnostic confusion with granulomatous infection requiring exclusion before immunosuppression
reference.prognosis: The disease is chronic; with prompt control of uveitis and arthritis, vision and joint function can be preserved, but delayed treatment risks permanent visual loss and joint damage, and some patients develop more extensive systemic involvement.
pitfalls: Labelling childhood granulomatous disease as ordinary sarcoidosis and missing the genetic diagnosis
Failing to screen for and aggressively treat asymptomatic uveitis
Starting immunosuppression before excluding granulomatous infection
Attributing the boggy synovitis to typical juvenile idiopathic arthritis
